_head_publish_why: Optional low-noise head hosting (#1 ask 6). head_publish_cmd runs after every publish_head(), throttled by head_publish_min_minutes, hard-timed-out, never fatal; the head file's path arrives as $SENTINEL_HEAD_PATH. Executes YOUR shell from YOUR config - same trust boundary as your plists; no default on purpose. Example: gh gist edit <gist-id> --filename sentinel-head.json "$SENTINEL_HEAD_PATH"
instance_purpose: Keep the declared targets healthy and the watchers honest.
_notification_mode_why: all keeps operational alerts and nightwatch reports; art-only suppresses every outbound message except a verified art deployment; off sends nothing. Art-only is for a creative collective whose only useful message is the final public work.
_report_number_why: iMessage/SMS destination for reports: nightwatch's play-by-play, and the evolve worker's one-text-per-verified-merge art update (title, tappable Pages URL, source, PR, one sentence). Falls back to notify_handle when unset.
_evolve_worker_why: Proactive art is a 15-30 minute model run; the health tick is every 15 minutes and launchd serialises it, so the two cannot share a clock without health losing. enabled:true moves the art arm to com.rapp.evolve-worker (evolve_worker.py + install-launchd.sh --with-evolve-worker) and the tick then spends NO model on art - diagnose/repair and repair_enabled are untouched. Omit the block, or leave enabled:false, and nothing about an existing install changes. degraded_allowlist is the ONLY way to evolve while degraded: every failing check id must be named there, and evolve_on_degraded is ignored by the worker. Two ids refuse to be allowlisted at all - alert_delivery (unverified or dead-lettered alerts mean the estate cannot reach a human) and health_runtime (the verdict is unknown). Listing them changes nothing: a loop that cannot report must not publish. The model works in a worker-made temp clone, may not commit/push/PR/merge, and the controller validates and owns every git and GitHub operation.
_evolve_worker_fanout_why: fanout spawns bounded read-only sub-sentinels before the maker runs: separate copilot processes, each with its own temp workspace, no git clone, no GitHub token in its environment, a hard timeout, its own process group, and RAPP_SENTINEL_DEPTH set so a child can never spawn children (max_depth 1). Each child returns one strict JSON report (rapp-subsentinel-report/1.0); the parent parses it deterministically, applies high-severity critiques as vetoes, and aggregates EXACTLY 10 finalists - which then must be round 1 of the submission's _dada_cycle. Fewer than 10 survivors, or fewer than min_healthy_children, fails the cycle out loud; a failed child is never an empty success. children is the cast size (max_children caps it, max_processes_per_cycle counts the maker too, daily_child_budget is a rolling 24h credit cap). Roles are configurable; wave 2 sees wave 1's candidates, which is what makes the adversarial verifier more than decoration. format_repair_attempts is 0 or 1 and nothing else: a child that answers with unparseable JSON gets at most one more process, and a config asking for more is rejected rather than quietly clamped.

evolve_worker._repo_why: owner/name, or a full https URL, or either with a .git suffix - normalised once into a transport URL for git and OWNER/REPO for gh, so the two never disagree.
evolve_worker._rapp_vision_why: Optional dual deployment. After the canonical Public Art Collective merge is re-read, the controller mirrors the exact gated bytes into a RAPP Vision channel, verifies that merge, waits for both GitHub Pages surfaces, and only then records success or sends the final links. A partial deployment stays pending and is retried before another model is spent.

roles.name: novelty-archaeologist
roles.brief: Dig through every prior submission before proposing anything; veto repeats.

roles.name: execution-designer
roles.brief: Think in the medium: a premise that cannot be built under 50 KB is a wish.

roles.name: adversarial-verifier
roles.brief: Attack wave one's candidates; a high-severity critique vetoes deterministically.

_commons_repo_why: owner/name of the commons this instance publishes art to. The evolve worker derives the merge notification's tappable URLs from it: https://<owner>.github.io/<name>/submissions/<slug>/piece.<ext> to view and https://github.com/<owner>/<name>/blob/<branch>/... for the source. Unset, a verified merge still texts you the PR link and says no public URL was derivable. Only a merge verified against fresh origin/main sends that message - never a model's SENTINEL_RESULT line, never an aborted or rejected cycle.
_watchers_why: health.py's probe_watchers reads its estate-probe targets from this block (issue #1 ask 2). Every key defaults to the previously hardcoded live values, so omitting the whole block changes nothing. Overrides merge per watcher - give only the keys you change. enabled:false skips that probe AND declares the omission in every verdict (w_checks_complete reports 'disabled by config'), never a silent green. openrappter.labels is the same key the spin scan unions into its candidate labels - one key, one read path.
_evolve_worker_confinement_why: Model processes get NO --allow-all. The maker gets bounded file tools (view/glob/grep/create/edit/write/apply_patch) rooted at --add-dir on its own workspace; sub-sentinels get --available-tools= (nothing at all) and answer in JSON on stdout. bash, powershell, fetch, web_search, task, ask_user and lsp are named in both --excluded-tools and --deny-tool; built-in MCPs, custom instructions, BASH_ENV, the system temp dir, remote control and auto-update are all switched off. HOME/XDG/TMPDIR/GH_CONFIG_DIR/git config point inside the workspace and the environment is an allowlist, so no operator credential is visible to a model. Inference auth is ONE variable (auth_env_var, default COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN) passed via --secret-env-vars so the CLI strips it from tool/MCP environments; with isolated_home true and that variable unset the cycle fails explicitly rather than falling back to your real ~/.copilot. sandbox_exec adds macOS sandbox-exec file-write confinement as defence in depth (off by default; tool and path limits are the mandatory layer). Its profile allows writes to exactly two roots - the sanitized staging directory and the sibling runtime directory holding the isolated HOME/XDG/TMPDIR - and never the controller's clone or your real HOME, so it REQUIRES isolated_home (and therefore auth_env_var); the combination sandbox_exec + shared HOME is refused up front rather than dying as a PermissionError. The clone is built by init + configured remote + fetch rather than `git clone` (which reads global config before resolving the url, so a url.<attacker>.insteadOf rewrite could redirect it), git itself is pinned to a trusted absolute binary (/usr/bin/git by default; git_binary may override it only if it resolves to a regular, executable, non-group/world-writable file under a trusted system root) so a fake `git` on PATH can never be chosen, PATH is SET to trusted system directories rather than inherited, and every controller git call runs in an environment built from an ALLOWLIST (locale, existing cert paths) so GIT_EXEC_PATH - which chooses git-remote-https and git-upload-pack - LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, proxies and anything a future git adds cannot arrive at all, with system/global config disabled apart from a generated file holding at most a validated credential helper, plus an isolated HOME/XDG/TMPDIR, allowed_repo_hosts plus a shape check validate the canonical url before git sees it, and every network git call (fetch, push, branch deletion) runs through one chokepoint that verifies repo integrity first; if the clone no longer verifies, an abandoned branch is deleted from the canonical URL through a fresh repository with global/system git config neutralised. The maker works in a SANITIZED STAGING directory - its read context plus a PRECREATED out/submission/ (it has file tools and no shell, so it can never create a directory; the slug lives in meta.json and the controller materialises submissions/<slug>/ in its own clone) - with no .git and no clone metadata in reach; the controller hashes the whole prepared staging tree before the model runs and afterwards requires every baseline path unchanged with only meta.json, one piece.<ext> and state-out.json as new paths (no new directories, hidden files, drafts or rewritten context), then copies only the two validated files into its own private clone, and immediately before every git operation it rejects any remote.origin.pushurl, unexpected local config, alternates or executable hooks and resets origin's fetch/push URLs to the configured repo. Only the controller has a shell, git and GitHub credentials.
_neighbor_cadence_why: Optional, per-slug, additive. The roster (`neighbors`) says WHO is seated; this says how often each declared slug must speak (max_stale_minutes, over the listed frame kinds or any) and - R2, ran is not worked - which kinds count as WORK and how long it may go without one (worked_kinds + max_unworked_minutes). w_neighbor_moving reads the slug's chain (never a heartbeat it could stamp) and fails at warn. Undeclared slugs keep the default behaviour: staleness never fails, only chain-break/truncation notifies. Example: an RBox author seated as `storyteller` that must speak every 90m and ship a book every 8h.
_hub_why: Optional, additive (hub.py). Sentinels installed from github.com/kody-w/rapp-sentinel-hub into HOME/hub/ (`python3 sentinel_sdk.py install @pub/slug_sentinel`) run every tick; their declared check ids JOIN the required set, so an installed sentinel that stops reporting fails w_checks_complete. Trust is a dial: a hub result's critical is demoted to warn (reason written into detail) unless its slug is in critical_allowed. config.<slug> merges over the file's manifest defaults; disabled skips a slug; unpaired_accepted accepts an R2 gap for a hub domain. Omit the whole block: nothing changes.
_evolve_worker_auth_why: Publishing needs credentials, and three live cycles made finished art before failing at `git push` with 'could not read Username'. The controller now GENERATES its own credential helper - a fixed `<validated gh> auth git-credential` given the operator's real HOME and validated gh config dir (default ~/.config/gh; gh_config_dir may override only with an absolute existing non-group/world-writable dir under the real home) - instead of inheriting whatever credential.helper the machine had. git keeps its isolated HOME and pinned config; GH_CONFIG_DIR is never in git's environment and never in any model's. Before a single child process runs, a preflight asks GitHub whether this account may push to the configured repo and asks `git credential fill` whether credentials actually resolve - lengths are logged, never values.
_evolve_worker_child_json_why: Children run with --output-format=json and answer in one typed assistant.message event; the parser accepts only that event, never reasoning, model.response, snapshots or stats (measured: a child's reasoning contains the same JSON as its answer, so scraping the last JSON-looking thing reads its thoughts as its reply). A reply that will not parse earns exactly one format-repair process - if the cycle deadline and max_processes_per_cycle allow - which is debited as a real spend and recorded; two bad replies fail the child, and a failed adversarial verifier still fails the cycle. Every attempt's transcript is kept under logs/subsentinels/<cycle>-<role>-<attempt>.log, bounded and redacted, outside the disposable workspace.
